page: Microsoft Azure D96ls_v7 is a compute-focused virtual machine belonging to the Dlsv7 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features a dedicated Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor with 96 vCPUs, mapped from 48 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. Operating at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz, the CPU is equipped with 48 KB L1D cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and a large 480 MB L3 cache. The system is configured with 192.0 GB of RAM, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of memory per core. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, though it is Premium Storage capable.

Benchmark results indicate strong multi-core performance and top-tier capabilities in specialized instruction sets. The server achieved a Passmark CPU score of 104,787.21 and a multi-core stress-ng score of 95,440.36. Its architectural support for advanced vector and matrix extensions, including AVX-512 and Intel AMX, is reflected in top-tier scores for extended instructions and encryption. Single-core performance is also notable, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2,224.0 and a gzip compression rate of 36.54 GB/sec. Memory bandwidth is robust, reaching 7,017.2 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 333.72 GB/sec for uncached large blocks, though the overall Passmark memory score remains average.

Given its high compute density and relatively low memory-to-vCPU ratio, the D96ls_v7 is highly cost-efficient for CPU-bound workloads that do not require massive memory footprints. It excels in software compilation, as demonstrated by a clang compilation score of 58,511.0, and multi-threaded decompression tasks. It is also well-suited for static web serving, Redis key-value stores, and medium-scale LLM inference, processing 7B model prompts at 304.72 tokens/second. Appropriate workloads include high-performance computing, CI/CD pipelines, web serving, and compute-heavy batch processing.
